text:
rachel-release: Canary in us-east failed validation during helm preflight -> deploy-bot held promotion: `deploy-bot: blocked - values schema mismatch (auth.enabled: expected boolean)`

devin.eng: I saw that locally too. The new chart v4.0.0 changed `auth.enabled` to a string ('on'/'off') for legacy reasons. Our release pipeline expects boolean.

sam.ops: So deploy-bot refuses to promote because CI preflight caught the schema drift. Good catch. Options: pin to v3.9.8, apply a values shim override converting 'on' -> true, or publish a patch v4.0.1 restoring boolean.

rachel-release: EU change windows later; current promotion batch includes us-east, eu-west. We need a quick decision to avoid blocking other unrelated services.

lee-sre: I'd prefer a shim override at deploy time: set `auth.enabled: true` in per-release values for blocked groups. It's reversible and faster than chart rollbacks.

mira-pm: If we do an override, note it in release notes: temporary compatibility shim due to schema change in v4.0.0. Also file follow-up to align chart changelog with schema changes.

devin.eng: I'll prepare the override snippet and attach to the release grouping. Snippet:
```yaml
auth:
  enabled: true
```
This will satisfy preflight and avoid touching migrations.

sam.ops: Applying override for groups: us-east, eu-west now.

deploy-bot: applying per-release override -> service/auth@2026-03-22-420 applied

deploy-bot: promotion resumed -> re-queueing groups (us-east, eu-west)

devin.eng: Canary in us-east passed post-upgrade checks after override. Confirming no pod restarts. :white_check_mark:

lee-sre: Follow-ups: 1) PR to chart repo to revert schema or add explicit deprecation path (v4.0.1), 2) add a CI schema contract test to detect type changes, 3) update release notes template to bold schema-breaking changes.

mira-pm: Release notes line: "Applied temporary per-release values shim to maintain boolean contract for auth.enabled while chart v4.0.0 schema is patched in v4.0.1."
